title: system design tradeoffs and decision methods
concepts: A tradeoff is a consequence of meeting one requirement under another constraint, not a slogan or a universal ranking. State the invariant and workload, compare mechanisms at the same abstraction level, then name operational and failure costs.
Translate product requirements into observable measures and testable user journeys before choosing components.
Make state ownership, consistency, replay, and recovery explicit at every boundary.
Account for latency, throughput, tail behavior, capacity, cost, security, privacy, and operational effort as interacting constraints.
Use a simple baseline, then add a mechanism only to meet a stated requirement or measured bottleneck.
Design failure behavior and release compatibility across client, API, data, and operations rather than per component.
